newsitem.title: CANADA: Oshawa Group net drops on start-up costs.
newsitem.headline: Oshawa Group net drops on start-up costs.

text.p: Supermarket and drugstore chain operator Oshawa Group Ltd said its second quarter profits dropped due to start-up costs for programs to strengthen retail competitiveness and streamline distribution.
Second quarter earnings fell to C$0.47 a share for the period ended August 10, compared to a year-earlier C$0.61 a share.
Oshawa Group also said it agreed to sell several real estate holdings. These gains will offset its full-year costs.
The company also said it is also is building a new distribution facility.

"The planned roll-out of a new point-of-sales electronic system, producing labor cost reductions and margin improvements, will be extended, beyond its current half-way point, to include all stores by year-end," Oshawa Group said.
Total cash used for investing activities rose to C$86.7 million in the second quarter, versus a year-earlier C$41.9 million.
Oshawa Group also hired former Wal-Mart Canada Inc president Bruce West in late August to turn around its floundering Pharma Plus Drug Mart chain.
